text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 2440 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- Prime Minister Gyula Horn Monday nominated Welfare Ministry Political State Secretary Mihaly Kokeny to the post of welfare minister.
- The opposition indicated it would not vote in favour of the ratification of the Romanian-Hungarian basic treaty.

- The economic cabinet passed the Finance Ministry's plan for a reform of the pension system to be submitted to Parliament in February. Employees would pay two-thirds of their pension contributions into a reformed pay-as-you-earn system, and one-third into a mandatory pension fund.

- Istvan Nikolits, minister responsible for overseeing the civil secret services, appeared before the parliamentary commission probing the "oilgate" affair on Monday, saying a legal basis underscored his placing of an 80-year stamp of secrecy on data in his letter to the commission.
- Akos Birtalan received the post of minister of tourism in the new Romanian cabinet Monday, while Gyorgy Tokay was named minister without portfolio for ethnic minority affairs.

- Minister of Industry, Trade and Tourism Szabolcs Fazekas taking part in the ongoing World Trade Organisation ministerial summit in Singapore, said Hungary is adopting a neutral stance regarding the global trade disputes which are splitting the developing and industrialised countries.
- The total amount of foreign currency purchased over the first ten months of this year, $316 million, was only about 50 percent of the figure in January-October 1995.
- The pace of wage increases slowed in October, putting an end to the tendency of escalating pay rises every month since June, the Central Statistical Office reports.
NEPSZABADSAG
- The Hungarian government will seek permission from Parliament to send a non-combat unit of up to 500 soldiers to carry out assignments as part of the SFOR mission.
- Hungarian unemployment levels will probably increase further despite prospects of economic growth, a study by the Labour Ministry concludes.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- The government's prognosis of 2-3 percent growth and 17 percent rate of infliation for 1997 is an illusion, said Jozsef Veres, president of the Hungarian Association of Economists.
- Hungary can again draw on a $90 million World Bank loan for road maintenance suspended early this year.
- After nearly two months' deliberations, the liquidation procedure of the refrigeration company Goldsun Rt. has begun.
NAPI GAZDASAG

- The deficit in the balance of payments came to $40 million in October. The total deficit in the first ten months of 1996 was $1.444 billion, nearly $1 billion less than over the same period last year.

- Significant changes will be made in the further privatisation of the energy sector and the strategy to sell off the broadcast firm Antenna Hungaria Rt, president of the State Privatisation and Holding Co. Arpad Kovacs announced.
- The privatisation contract of Magyar Hitel Bank is to be signed in Budapest on December 18 by leaders of the Dutch bank ABN Amro and Hungarian Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy.
MAGYAR NEMZET
- Deputy spokesman Andras Rozsa has been promoted to police spokesman.
